headline: Default pairwise risks are mostly low-to-medium; the main concern is shared-document prompt injection and workflow confusion, not direct exfiltration.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU can ingest local PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes an MCP server; pdf.js runs in a browser-based worker and handles PDF files. If outputs from MinerU are fed into pdf.js through a shared file or browser workflow, attacker-controlled document content could be misread as instructions. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so I choose medium.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into pdf.js as trusted text or annotations
IF both agents share a workspace where document content is later interpreted as instructions
mitigations: Disable any workflow that treats extracted text as commands
Separate input and review folders for the two agents
Require human review before reusing extracted text
Add a fixed prompt prefix that labels all imported content as untrusted
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to extracted fields

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, images, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, and OCR text, while pdf.js only touches PDF documents and has no network egress. With no shared workspace or upload path documented, there is no clear default leakage route between them. The main risk is local file exposure if an operator manually reuses the same sensitive PDFs in both tools.
conditions: IF the same sensitive PDF is opened in both tools on a shared workstation
IF extracted text from MinerU is manually pasted into pdf.js-related notes or logs
mitigations: Use separate folders for each agent
Avoid copying extracted text into shared notes
Delete temporary exports after review
Restrict access to sensitive source files
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and pdf.js has no write, git, or network-write capability listed. That makes direct resource contention unlikely. The only overlap is read/processing of PDFs, so conflict is limited to benign concurrent access rather than destructive mutation.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same PDF file simultaneously
IF the operator expects one agent to mutate shared state for the other
mitigations: Open read-only copies of source PDFs
Avoid concurrent edits to shared directories
Run each agent in its own working folder
Close one agent before batch-processing with the other

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, formulas, and OCR output that pdf.js could plausibly consume in a browser-based workflow. If pdf.js treats MinerU output as authoritative without verification, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect rendering or downstream decisions. The pathway is plausible from the profiles, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF pdf.js consumes MinerU-extracted text or metadata without validation
IF downstream users rely on the combined output for decisions
mitigations: Add a verification step between extraction and rendering
Compare a sample of outputs against the source PDF
Flag low-confidence OCR fields for review
Keep original PDFs alongside derived artifacts
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for exchanged data

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are document-processing tools with no requested OAuth scopes or secrets handled, and both profiles show no explicit residency or retention mismatch. The remaining compliance concern is operational: sensitive PDFs may be processed by two separate open-source tools, but the profiles do not show a direct policy conflict. I therefore rate this low and cite both profiles for the shared data class.
conditions: IF regulated documents are routed through both tools without an approved retention policy
IF the operator stores derived outputs longer than the source policy allows
mitigations: Confirm retention settings before processing regulated files
Delete derived artifacts after review
Use a documented data-handling SOP
Limit processing to non-regulated documents
requires-engineering: add policy-based retention controls
